rows: KidsFirst; existing annotations from J:15425, J:98554 annotations are scattered under various terms, https://github.com/mgijax/mammalian-phenotype-ontology/issues/3511

KidsFirst; The MP term definition for chordee MP:0003555 specifies acute angulation of the penis upon erection and places chordee under abnormal penile erection MP:0001379, unlike HPO which places Chordee HP:0000041 under Abnormal penis morphology HP:0000036 and provides details on the direction of bowing and degree of angulation. I think the match is therefore close and the MP term should be placed under both abnormal penile erection and morphology (see https://educalingo.com/en/dic-en/chordee)
KidsFirst; absence of both kidneys, HPO term has child terms for bilateral and unilateral renal agenesis that would be exact matches to the MP terms
KidsFirst; MP specifies size not circumference and does not specify how much smaller
HPO term has specifics for when this would be called in humans that I interpret as more extreme than how the MP term would be applied

Some terms came from more than one source. The KidsFirst list was a list of HPO terms provided by the KidsFirst team from the set of terms used for patients in their cohorts. The scoliosis, Alzheimer, cleft palate, Down Syndrome, CHARGE Syndrome, Cornelia De Lange Syndrome, and COVID term sets were generated by MGI for symptoms or phenotypes associated with the disease. For the COVID set the references for each sign or symptom are listed in the Other column. Initially the mapping dates for the KidsFirst mappings were not tracked, so these were given the date of when we received the file (5/27/21).  The scoliosis, cleft palate, Down Syndrome, CHARGE Syndrome, and Cornelia De Lange Syndrome sets consist of MP terms that are associated with mouse models of scoliosis. For Down Syndrome, CHARGE Syndrome, and Cornelia De Lange Syndrome HPO terms associated with each disease were also pulled from the HPO files for mapping. The Alzheimer and COVID sets were created by identifying symptoms and signs for patients from the literature then identifying the relevant MP and HP terms and finally mapping the identified terms to terms in the other ontology. Use of skos mappings terms: exact match: MP term is the same as the HPO term, ignoring that the HP term applies only to humans; broad match: HPO term covers more than the MP term, ignoring the species restriction; narrow match: HPO term is more restricted than the MP term; related match: MP term and HPO term share some similarity but would not have a parent-child relation in a shared ontology.
metadata.mapping_set_title: All mappings of MP terms to HPO terms generated by MGI

rows: KidsFirst; existing annotations from J:15425, J:98554 annotations are scattered under various terms, https://github.com/mgijax/mammalian-phenotype-ontology/issues/3511

KidsFirst; The MP term definition for chordee MP:0003555 specifies acute angulation of the penis upon erection and places chordee under abnormal penile erection MP:0001379, unlike HPO which places Chordee HP:0000041 under Abnormal penis morphology HP:0000036 and provides details on the direction of bowing and degree of angulation. I think the match is therefore close and the MP term should be placed under both abnormal penile erection and morphology (see https://educalingo.com/en/dic-en/chordee)
KidsFirst; absence of both kidneys, HPO term has child terms for bilateral and unilateral renal agenesis that would be exact matches to the MP terms
KidsFirst; MP specifies size not circumference and does not specify how much smaller
HPO term has specifics for when this would be called in humans that I interpret as more extreme than how the MP term would be applied
